title: seek configuration file
description: The JSON object seek reads from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/seek/config.json, or ~/.config/seek/config.json when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is empty or unset. Its keys are seek's variable names, and an environment variable with the same name takes precedence over the file. A Vault or OpenBao secret read through SEEK_VAULT_PATH holds fields with these same names. seek reads string values only and ignores other keys.

PARALLEL_API_KEY.description: Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`. A seek server sends it to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header.

EXA_API_KEY.description: Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`. A seek server sends it to Exa as the `x-api-key` header.

BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY.description: Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header.

BRAVE_ANSWERS_API_KEY.description: Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header.

PERPLEXITY_API_KEY.description: Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`. A seek server sends it to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

GEMINI_API_KEY.description: Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`. A seek server sends it to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header.

FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.description: Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`. A seek server sends it to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

SEEK_SERVER_URL.description: Base URL of a seek server. When it is set, the CLI sends every provider call to `<url>/v1/proxy/<upstream>` with the client token, and does not use local provider keys. The value is trimmed and trailing slashes are removed.

SEEK_SERVER_TOKEN.description: Client token for a seek server. The CLI sends the whole value as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, so a client's value is one token. `seek serve` accepts each entry of a comma-separated list, which allows rotation.

additionalProperties.description: seek ignores keys it does not read.
